FOR AGENTS

A cleaner desk: the left cards, top bar and lists keep their words on one line, long names are shortened with the full name on hover, loading shows placeholders instead of jumping, and motion is short and switches off where your device asks for less.

The email AI's draft on the desk: an email that belongs to a ticket now shows the AI's draft reply right above the reply box, with Approve and send and Discard, not only on the ticket's own page.

What is waiting: "waiting in my queues" now says what is waiting, for example "(1 Voice · 2 Email · 1 Ticket)".

New message for agents: an agent is offered only the email, WhatsApp, SMS and social accounts of the queues they work in. Supervisors and administrators still see every account.

Social comments: on Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok and LinkedIn you can like and, where your organisation allows it, delete a comment, and start a direct message within each network's window.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS AND SUPERVISORS

Ticket rules: rules can now email the customer, a team or chosen addresses, notify people, call a webhook and close a ticket with a resolution code, and can look at the channel a ticket came in by, the requester's email and your business hours. Nineteen ready-made rules in four packs are added switched off, and Ticket settings' reminder and automatic close can move into rules in one click. Macros can carry files and are suggested by contact reason.

Ticket forms: a field can show only when another field has a chosen value (for example "Printer model" when the category is Printer); hidden fields are never required. Ticket fields can be used as breakdowns and filters in your own reports.

Help centres: your own page templates, five ready-made looks, articles in the reader's language, sections shared between help centres, and a question before the request form that answers from your articles. The website chat can open with your help centre first.

Social channels: Connect with Facebook to choose your Pages instead of pasting tokens, and connect X, TikTok and LinkedIn with your own developer access. Comment rules can hide, flag or prioritise comments, and the account list warns when a network stops accepting your keys.

Verified callers: with "Require verification before showing masked customer details" on, the desk's chats, tickets, history, search and lists keep contact details back until the caller is verified; names stay visible, and a customer verified in the last hour shows in full.

Wallboards that fit: a wallboard or a dashboard on a wall always fits the screen; when there are too many tiles it turns pages every 15 seconds instead of scrolling.

A cleaner console: tables, figures and page headers are tidier, row actions no longer run off the edge, and the Floor's agent tiles use the full width.

Email signatures for teams: give a team or a mailbox one standard HTML signature, filled in for each person with their name, title, phone, mobile and email. Start from the ready-made "Yaxxa standard" under Settings → Email signatures, and fill in people's titles and numbers under People's details (agents can fill in their own on the desk).

Floor by queue: choosing a queue beside Floor narrows the whole floor to it, counting agents by teams, the skills the queue needs and moves. The Floor's red "breached" figure now opens the work that went over its service level today, finished or not.

Duplicate tickets: a client's reply that is already on a ticket now points the agent to that ticket, and a second ticket on the same email is refused unless opened as a separate matter. Tickets that look like duplicates show Possible duplicate with Merge.
